root.label: Integer arithmetic and overflow
root.note: Unsigned wraps by definition; signed overflow is undefined; promotion hides which one you are doing.

children.label: Overflow contracts
children.note: Unsigned arithmetic is modular; signed overflow leaves the language rules.

children.label: Unsigned wraparound
children.note: Results are reduced modulo 2 to the width, so UINT_MAX + 1u is 0.

children.label: Signed overflow
children.note: Undefined behavior under [expr.pre]; compilers may assume it never happens.

children.label: Two's complement, C++20
children.note: The representation is now fixed, but signed overflow is still undefined.

children.label: Constant evaluation
children.note: Overflow in a constexpr initializer is not a constant expression, so it is diagnosed.

children.label: Promotion trap
children.note: Narrow unsigned operands become int before arithmetic.

children.label: unsigned short product
children.note: Both operands promote to int, so 65535 * 65535 overflows with a 32-bit int.

children.label: The fix
children.note: Cast an operand to unsigned first, or write 1u * a * b.

children.label: Division and remainder
children.note: Quotients truncate toward zero and the remainder follows the dividend.

children.label: Truncation, C++11
children.note: -7 / 2 is -3 and -7 % 2 is -1; (a / b) * b + a % b equals a.

children.label: INT_MIN / -1
children.note: The quotient does not fit, so both division and remainder are undefined.

children.label: Division by zero
children.note: Undefined for both / and %.

children.label: abs(INT_MIN)
children.note: The result is not representable, so the behavior is undefined.

children.label: Comparing integers
children.note: Mixed-sign comparison converts to unsigned; C++20 adds value-based helpers.

children.label: -1 < 1u is false
children.note: The signed operand converts to unsigned, so -1 becomes UINT_MAX.

children.label: cmp_less family
children.note: std::cmp_* compare mathematical values; they reject char types and bool.

children.label: in_range
children.note: std::in_range<R>(v) tells whether v fits in type R without converting it.

children.label: ssize and loops
children.note: Use std::ssize or i-- > 0 to avoid size_t underflow in reverse loops.

children.label: Conversions
children.note: Conversion to unsigned is modular; to signed it is modular since C++20.

children.label: Narrowing to signed
children.note: 200 to int8_t is -56 in C++20; it was implementation-defined before.

children.label: List-initialization
children.note: Narrowing is ill-formed unless the source is a constant that fits.

children.label: Safe arithmetic, C++26
children.note: Library tools that handle overflow without undefined behavior.

children.label: Saturating operations
children.note: C++26 clamps to the type's limits; libstdc++ 16 spells them saturating_add and so on.

children.label: ckd_add and ckd_mul
children.note: From <stdckdint.h>: return true on overflow and store the wrapped result.

children.label: Compiler builtins
children.note: __builtin_add_overflow does the same job in GCC and Clang today.
